pages.text: A superconducting heavy-ion linac (40 niobium cavities) fires a projectile into an actinide target. Fuse just above the Coulomb barrier with the compound nucleus cool enough to survive: one atom at a time, the island of stability.

$(thing)Set$(): Cavity voltage V, Synchronous phase φ, Ion charge state, Beam intensity, Solenoid field.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Cavity field drift (microphonics, Lorentz detuning): every cavity gives V·(1 ± 1%·d).

$(thing)Limits$(): Interlock: niobium cavities not superconducting; Cavity quench: the niobium went normal; Phase at the crest: no phase focusing, the bunch spreads out; Below the Coulomb barrier: nothing fuses; Solenoids too weak to focus the beam; Interlock: focusing solenoids not superconducting (too warm).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Fusions per second: beam intensity × transmission × cross-section.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Effective cavity voltage: V_eff = V·(1 + δ)$(br)Beam energy (lab): E_lab = N·q·V·cos φ$(br)Centre-of-mass energy: E_cm = E_lab·A_t/(A_p + A_t)$(br)Coulomb barrier: V_C = 1.44·Z₁Z₂ / R  (MeV·fm)$(br)Excitation energy E*: E* = E_cm + Q$(br)Relative cross-section: σ/σ_max = e^−((E*−E*_opt)/5)²$(br)Linac transmission: T ≈ 3·sin|φ|
